title: Ambition Content Briefs: Weeks 1-2
summary: First two weeks of content briefs for Ambition Mechanical social media.
content:
Ambition Mechanical Content Briefs -- Weeks 1-2

Created: 2026-03-09 Client: Ambition Mechanical Contact: Marlon (owner) Vertical: Commercial mechanical construction (HVAC, plumbing, piping) Platforms: Instagram, TikTok (5 Reels/week), LinkedIn (2/week) Footage source: /Users/patrik/Ahead of Market Dropbox/AOM/Client/Ambition Mechanical Services/VIDEO/ Status: Briefs ready. 6 files downloaded, 82 cloud-only. Briefs reference available footage where possible.

How to Use These Briefs

  • Briefs 1-14: Instagram/TikTok Reels (5/week x 2 weeks + 4 extras for scheduling flexibility)
  • Briefs 15-18: LinkedIn posts (2/week x 2 weeks)
  • Each brief references specific downloaded files where applicable
  • Where footage isn't available yet, the brief describes what's needed so filming can be targeted
  • Output to projects/content-agent/output/ambition/

WEEK 1 -- REELS (Instagram + TikTok)

Reel 01: Emergency Response Story

Concept: Ambition's reliability in a crisis. Emergency work = trust content. This is the strongest narrative hook in the downloaded footage.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 20-30s Edit pattern: Problem/Solution

Hook: On-screen text: "3AM call. They needed us." Open on dark/dramatic shot from the footage. Body: Show the emergency response work. What was broken, how Ambition showed up, what they fixed. Fast cuts through the work. CTA: "When it matters, Ambition shows up. 24/7."

Footage file: Abraza / Abraza Emergency Response.mov (35s, 16:9, needs vertical crop) Crop note: Center-crop 16:9 to 9:16. Review the frame to confirm important action stays in center. If not, use pan-and-scan. Music: Dramatic intro, resolves to confident energy. Captions: On-screen text throughout. Story-driven: "The call came in at [X]." / "Ambition was on site in [X] hours." / "Fixed." Voice: Consider ElevenLabs VO using AMBITION MECHANICAL voice (WkvyyiDC9ciaSfbQ8bxp) for the narrative.

Reel 02: Primrose Progress Update (Cut Down)

Concept: Progress update on the Primrose job site. This file is already vertical and edited. Tighten it to the 30s sweet spot and add modern social formatting.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 30-40s (trimmed from 1:37) Edit pattern: Time-Lapse Progress / Before/After

Hook: Open on the most impressive wide shot of the Primrose site. On-screen text: "Primrose. In progress." Body: Pull the best 30 seconds from the 97-second file. Focus on visual variety: wide shots, detail work, crew in frame. Cut anything that drags. CTA: "Another one coming together. #commercialconstruction"

Footage file: Primrose / Primerose Update .mov (1:37, already 9:16 vertical) Crop note: None needed. Already vertical. Music: Confident, steady energy. Construction rhythms. Captions: Project name + progress milestones as text overlays. Add captions for any spoken audio.

Reel 03: Din Tai Fung Kitchen Build -- The Scale

Concept: Show the scale of building a commercial kitchen for a major restaurant brand. Din Tai Fung is a recognizable name. Leverage it.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 25-35s Edit pattern: Behind the Scenes

Hook: On-screen text: "Building a kitchen for Din Tai Fung." Cut immediately to a wide shot showing the scope. Body: Pull the most impressive sequences from the kitchen footage. Pipes, ductwork, mechanical systems. The complexity that most people never see. CTA: "This is what commercial mechanical looks like. #HVAC #construction"

Footage file: Din Tai Fung at Scottsdale FS / DIN TAI Kitchen.mov (1:31, 16:9) Crop note: Center-crop to 9:16. Kitchen footage may work well in vertical since equipment is tall. Music: Industrial, modern. Clean energy. Captions: "Din Tai Fung. Scottsdale Fashion Square." + technical callouts on specific systems visible.

Reel 04: "What Commercial Mechanical Actually Looks Like"

Concept: Educational content. Most people don't know what mechanical contractors do. Demystify it. Position Ambition as the expert.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 20-30s Edit pattern: Educational / Quick Tip

Hook: On-screen text: "Most people have no idea what a mechanical contractor does." Body: Quick cuts showing the range: HVAC systems, plumbing, piping, ductwork. Each clip gets a text label. CTA: "Now you know. Follow for more."

Footage files: Mix clips from multiple downloaded files. Pull 2-3 second segments showing different types of work:

  • Din Tai Fung at Scottsdale FS / |+.mov (1:44, 16:9) -- general construction progress
  • Din Tai Fung at Scottsdale FS / DIN TAI Kitchen.mov -- kitchen mechanical
  • INEOS Grenadier / Arrowhead.mov -- commercial work
  • _WEBSITE / Website Background.mov -- best-of compilation shots Music: Clean, modern, informational. Captions: Text labels on each system: "HVAC" / "Plumbing" / "Piping" / "Sheet Metal"

Reel 05: Arrowhead Project Highlight

Concept: Showcase the INEOS Grenadier / Arrowhead project. At 52s this is already close to social length. Tighten and format for vertical.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 25-35s (trimmed from 52s) Edit pattern: Problem/Solution or Before/After (depends on footage content)

Hook: Open on the most visually striking shot from the file. On-screen text: project name. Body: Best 25 seconds of the work. Focus on scale, precision, and the finished result. CTA: "500+ projects completed. Ambition Mechanical."

Footage file: INEOS Grenadier / Arrowhead.mov (52s, 16:9) Crop note: Center-crop to 9:16. Review for framing. Music: Confident, premium feel. Matches the brand credibility of INEOS Grenadier. Captions: Project name + location as lower third.

WEEK 1 -- LINKEDIN

LinkedIn 01: Din Tai Fung Case Study

Concept: LinkedIn-formatted deep dive on the Din Tai Fung kitchen build. Show the complexity, the timeline, the result. Decision-makers on LinkedIn want substance.

Format: 16:9 landscape (LinkedIn native) Length: 45-60s Edit pattern: Process Breakdown

Hook: "Building a commercial kitchen for Din Tai Fung. Here's what it took." Body: Walk through the project phases. Show the mechanical systems, the coordination, the scale. Slower pacing than Reels. Let the work speak. CTA: "Looking for a mechanical contractor who delivers at this level? Let's talk."

Footage files:

  • Din Tai Fung at Scottsdale FS / |+.mov (1:44, 16:9) -- full project overview
  • Din Tai Fung at Scottsdale FS / DIN TAI Kitchen.mov (1:31, 16:9) -- kitchen-specific Crop note: None. 16:9 is native to LinkedIn. Music: Subtle, professional. Underscore, not feature. Captions: Essential. 80%+ of LinkedIn video is watched muted. Full on-screen text for every key point. Include project stats if available. Post copy: "When Din Tai Fung needed a mechanical partner for their Scottsdale Fashion Square location, they needed precision, speed, and reliability. Here's a look at what that actually takes behind the walls. #commercialconstruction #HVAC #mechanicalcontractor"

LinkedIn 02: "Why Commercial Mechanical Is the Backbone of Every Build"

Concept: Thought leadership. Marlon or the Ambition brand explaining why mechanical work matters, even though it's invisible once the walls close up.

Format: 16:9 or 1:1 Length: 30-60s Edit pattern: Educational / Quick Tip

Hook: "You'll never see our work once the building opens. Here's why it's the most important part." Body: Show mechanical systems being installed, then walls going up over them. The contrast between visible and invisible. Pull from any available footage. CTA: "The work you don't see is the work that matters most."

Footage files: Mix from _WEBSITE / Website Background.mov (best-of shots) + any construction progress footage from other files. Music: Understated, confident. Captions: Full on-screen text. Written for muted viewing. Post copy: "Mechanical systems are the first thing installed and the last thing anyone sees. HVAC, plumbing, piping. It's all behind the walls. But when it fails, everyone notices. That's why we don't cut corners. 200+ facilities. 500+ projects. The work speaks for itself. #mechanicalcontractor #commercialconstruction" Voice: Strong candidate for AMBITION MECHANICAL ElevenLabs voice narration.

WEEK 2 -- REELS (Instagram + TikTok)

Reel 06: Website Background Remix -- Best Shots Compilation

Concept: The website background video is a curated reel of Ambition's best visuals. Repurpose it as a social-first compilation with modern formatting.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-25s Edit pattern: Before/After or Time-Lapse (compilation style)

Hook: No text for first 2 seconds. Just the most visually striking shot. Then: "Ambition Mechanical." Body: Fastest, most dynamic clips from the website background. Recut for vertical with tight pacing. 1.5-2s per clip. CTA: "This is what we build."

Footage file: _WEBSITE / Website Background.mov (35s, 16:9) Crop note: Center-crop to 9:16. These are already the best shots, so framing should work. Music: High energy, beat-matched cuts. Captions: Minimal. Brand name + "Commercial Mechanical Contractor" at the end.

Reel 07: Primrose Part 2 -- Detail Work

Concept: Second cut from the Primrose footage, this time focused on close-up detail work. The precision angle.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-25s Edit pattern: Behind the Scenes

Hook: Close-up of hands working. Pipe fitting, welding, measuring. No text initially. Body: All detail shots. The craftsmanship. Then pull back to reveal the full scope. CTA: "Precision at scale. That's the Ambition standard."

Footage file: Primrose / Primerose Update .mov -- pull different segments than Reel 02. Focus on close-ups and detail work. Music: Subtle, precise. Match the attention-to-detail angle. Captions: Technical callouts on what's being done in each clip.

Reel 08: "Day on a Commercial Job Site" (Needs New Footage)

Concept: Day-in-the-life format. Follow the Ambition crew through a day. This is the content type that builds the strongest audience connection.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 30-45s Edit pattern: Day in the Life / POV

Hook: 6 AM energy. Truck pulling up, boots on ground, walking to the site. Body: Morning briefing, work begins, crew in action, lunch break moment, afternoon push, end-of-day walkthrough. CTA: "Another day, another build. #dayinthelife #construction"

Footage needed: THIS REQUIRES NEW FILMING. Shoot vertical (9:16) from the start. Need: arrival, setup, work sequences, crew moments, end-of-day. Ideally Marlon on camera at some point. Music: Building energy throughout the day arc. Captions: Time stamps on screen: "6:00 AM" / "10:00 AM" / "3:00 PM" / "Done."

Reel 09: Client Name-Drop Compilation

Concept: Ambition works with recognizable brands. Show the logos, show the work, build credibility fast. Din Tai Fung, INEOS, Abraza, Primrose.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-20s Edit pattern: Before/After (reputation build)

Hook: On-screen text: "Some of our recent projects." Body: Quick cuts: 2-3 seconds per project. Project name on screen. Best visual from each. Rapid, confident. CTA: "Trusted by the brands that matter. ambitionmechanical.com"

Footage files: Pull one strong clip from each downloaded file:

  • Abraza / Abraza Emergency Response.mov
  • Din Tai Fung at Scottsdale FS / DIN TAI Kitchen.mov
  • INEOS Grenadier / Arrowhead.mov
  • Primrose / Primerose Update .mov Music: Premium, confident. Quick cuts on beats. Captions: Project name as large text overlay per clip. End with Ambition logo.

Reel 10: "What's Behind Your Walls" -- Shock/Curiosity

Concept: Curiosity-driven content. Show what mechanical systems look like before drywall closes everything up. Most people have no idea.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-25s Edit pattern: Educational / Quick Tip + Shock/Surprise

Hook: On-screen text: "You're not supposed to see this." Open on exposed mechanical systems. Body: Pan through exposed HVAC, piping, ductwork. Text labels on each system. Then show the finished wall going up over all of it. CTA: "This is what's behind your walls. And it better be done right."

Footage files: Any clips showing exposed mechanical systems before walls are closed. Pull from:

  • Din Tai Fung at Scottsdale FS / |+.mov
  • Din Tai Fung at Scottsdale FS / DIN TAI Kitchen.mov
  • Additional footage needed for the "wall closing" payoff shot Music: Mysterious/curiosity intro, resolves to confident. Captions: System labels. Educational formatting.

WEEK 2 -- LINKEDIN

LinkedIn 03: Emergency Response Case Study

Concept: LinkedIn-formatted story about the Abraza emergency response. Decision-makers want to know their mechanical contractor shows up when it counts.

Format: 16:9 landscape Length: 30-45s Edit pattern: Problem/Solution

Hook: "When Abraza needed emergency mechanical response, we were on site in hours." Body: Show the problem, the response, the fix. Slower pacing than the Reel version (Brief 01). Add context and substance. CTA: "Reliability isn't a marketing line. It's a track record."

Footage file: Abraza / Abraza Emergency Response.mov (35s, 16:9) Crop note: None needed. 16:9 native. Music: Subtle, professional. Captions: Full on-screen text. Timeline overlay: "Hour 1" / "Hour 4" / "Resolved." Post copy: "Emergency mechanical work isn't something you plan for. It's something you need the right partner for. When Abraza called, Ambition was on site and working within hours. Not days, not 'we'll get back to you.' Hours. That's what 500+ projects and 20+ years in the field looks like in practice. #emergencyrepair #mechanicalcontractor #commercialconstruction"

LinkedIn 04: "The Projects Behind the Brands You Know"

Concept: Portfolio credibility piece. Show that Ambition works with name brands. LinkedIn audience responds to recognizable logos and institutional trust.

Format: 16:9 or 1:1 Length: 45-60s Edit pattern: Behind the Scenes + Testimonial tone

Hook: "You've been to these places. You've never seen what's behind the walls." Body: Walk through 3-4 projects with name recognition. Din Tai Fung, INEOS, Ritz Carlton (if footage downloads). Show the mechanical work that makes these spaces function. CTA: "The work you don't see is what makes everything work."

Footage files:

  • Din Tai Fung at Scottsdale FS / DIN TAI Kitchen.mov
  • INEOS Grenadier / Arrowhead.mov
  • Abraza / Abraza Emergency Response.mov
  • Additional files if downloaded: Memorial Tower, Teleferic, Ritz Carlton Music: Premium, brand-level. Confident without being flashy. Captions: Brand names as text overlays. Stats where available. Post copy: "Din Tai Fung. INEOS. Abraza. Ritz Carlton. Memorial Tower Senior Apartments. These are places people know. And behind every wall, above every ceiling, under every floor, there's mechanical work that makes them function. HVAC. Plumbing. Piping. It's not glamorous. It's essential. Ambition Mechanical has been delivering this work across the Valley for 20+ years. 500+ projects. 200+ facilities. The brands trust us because the work speaks for itself. #mechanicalcontractor #commercialconstruction #HVAC" Voice: Strong candidate for AMBITION MECHANICAL ElevenLabs narration.

Overflow Reels (Week 2 extras for scheduling flexibility)

Reel 11: Drone Reveal (Needs Cloud Download)

Concept: Dramatic drone reveal of a job site. Crane and drone footage is the highest-engagement content in construction social media.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-20s Edit pattern: Shock/Surprise

Hook: Drone rising over the job site. No text for 3 seconds. Let the scale hit. Body: Full drone reveal, then cut to ground-level crew footage for contrast. CTA: "Building the Valley, one project at a time."

Footage needed: Download from cloud: Ritz Carlton folder has DJI drone files. Memorial Tower "Crane Day" files. Any aerial footage. Music: Cinematic. The drone shot needs audio weight.

Reel 12: "500+ Projects" Stats Reel (Needs Confirmation)

Concept: Fast-paced stats reel. Numbers build credibility. Visual proof behind each stat.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 15-20s Edit pattern: Before/After (credibility build)

Hook: "500+ projects." (big text, visual hit) Body: "200+ facilities." / "20+ years." / "24/7 emergency response." Each stat gets 3 seconds and a matching clip. CTA: "Ambition Mechanical. ambitionmechanical.com"

Footage files: One clip per stat from any downloaded footage. Note: Confirm stats with client before publishing. Currently waiting on client confirmation per punch list. Music: Impactful, beat-matched to stat reveals.

Reel 13: Crew at Work -- No Words Needed (Needs New Footage)

Concept: Pure visual content. No text, no narration. Just the crew doing the work. The footage IS the content. Algorithm loves high watch-time, low-friction content.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 20-30s Edit pattern: Day in the Life

Hook: Open on hands working. Wrench turning, pipe being fitted, welding spark. Body: Sequence of work clips. All close-up and medium shots. Faces and hands. The craftsmanship. CTA: None on screen. Caption only: "The work speaks."

Footage needed: Close-up footage of crew working. Hands, tools, materials. Shot vertical from the start. Music: Lo-fi or ambient. Let the natural sounds of work come through.

Reel 14: Marlon On Camera -- Meet the Owner (Needs New Footage)

Concept: Put a face on Ambition. Marlon speaking directly to camera about what Ambition does and why they do it differently. Founder content performs at 2-3x engagement vs brand content.

Format: Reel (9:16) Length: 30-45s Edit pattern: Testimonial (self-testimonial)

Hook: Marlon mid-sentence with the strongest soundbite. Never start with "Hi, I'm Marlon." Body: Marlon talking about Ambition's approach. Intercut with b-roll of job sites, crew working, finished projects. CTA: "That's Ambition. Link in bio."

Footage needed: THIS REQUIRES NEW FILMING. Marlon on camera, speaking naturally. Shoot vertical. B-roll from existing downloaded files to intercut. Music: Subtle underneath. Marlon's voice is the feature.

Priority Download List (Cloud Files That Unlock More Content)

To keep this content calendar running past week 2, download these files next:

  1. Memorial Tower Senior Apts (14 files) -- crane content, serialized pipe setup, multiple formats. 2+ weeks of content alone.
  2. Teleferic (6 files) -- crane day + social-formatted edits already exist.
  3. _LABORERS (2 files) -- crew/people content. Essential for crew culture briefs.
  4. _WEBSITE / 2025 RECAP -- highlight reel for mining clips.
  5. Ritz Carlton (4 files) -- high-end brand credibility + drone footage.
  6. Din Tai Fung remaining (16 files) -- laborers series = people content.
